question: Should exec denylist policy be persisted in both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json, or should one surface be the canonical owner?
rationale: This choice defines the permanent security-policy ownership, migration, UI, hot-reload, and compatibility contract across gateway, node, and macOS execution.

options.title: Single approval-policy owner
options.body: Keep the denylist in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface, preserving one mutable authorization source.

options.title: Dual unioned surfaces
options.body: Adopt both surfaces permanently and document and test their precedence, hot reload, migration, and editing ownership.

recommendation.title: Single approval-policy owner
recommendation.body: Keep the denylist in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface, preserving one mutable authorization source.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent adjacent work established the delayed macOS execution-authorization ownership and snapshot contract extended by this decision.
